Actor behavior is consistent with the specified roles and reliability, and consequences reflect an asymmetry that penalizes false positives more than lenient treatment of low-signal cases. Rendering instructions are followed closely: each round includes the full consequence/context/resource/actors chain, no extraneous confounds are introduced, events are described concretely rather than via variable labels, and temporal continuity between rounds is preserved. Minor limitations—such as only early-stage illustration of delayed feedback and cost asymmetry—are inherent to the short horizon and do not materially contaminate the behavioral test, so the simulation remains highly valid overall.
